CFD_Automation · Stage 1 · geometry · code 0.6.0

Wing Generator

Eighteen numbers go in; one exact wing surface comes out, measured, labelled and checked. One generator and one YAML file make BWB, cranked, tapered and flying wings, sized like real Class I and II UAVs. Every later stage (mesh, solver, data) reads only this surface.

At a glanceParametersSizesRe and MachFlow phenomenaWhere to refineFix before Stage 2Design decisionsReal wings and ReChecks and resultsOpen decisionsWhat it cannot makePublished wingsCommands

At a glance

In

18 numbers + a wing type

From configs/wing.yaml: chords, spans, sweeps, twists, dihedrals, and an airfoil per station. Types: BWB, cranked, tapered, flying wing.

Out

One surface, checked

Upper, lower and trailing-edge base, read as upper(u, v). Plus measured values, labels, four refusing checks, a hash, IGES.

Evidence

730 of 730 wings pass

Sampled wings of all four types, 0 refused (code 0.6.0, numpy loft). 7 of 7 published wings verified. Tests: 140 pass without pyGeo, 11 more need pyGeo (run 30 Oct 2026).

Verdict

Ready for Stage 2 after the pyGeo run

Fixes 1 and 2 done (panel dihedrals, code hash). Left: run the pyGeo tests and rebuild the sets with pyGeo on your machine; fix 3 belongs to the mesher. Not yet "any wing": straight panels only, no airfoil shape variable. Sets: built with the current code, loft backend: numpy.

Parameters: inputs and derived

The generator samples only the inputs below. Everything else is derived from them by fixed formulas. Four stations: root b0, breaks b1 and b2, tip b3; three straight panels between them.

Full space

What we support

Wider ranges and every sourced airfoil. Sampled sparsely: 40 wings per type, plus both corner sets at its edges. Grey line in each cell.

Focus space

Where real wings are

Ranges from real Class I–II wings and papers; suggested airfoils. Sampled densely: 100 wings per type, the reference wings and the hold-out. Bold line in each cell.

Why two

Wide, but dense where it counts

The mesher must work on anything we claim to support; the studies and the ML spend most runs where real wings are. The focus box lies inside the full box (the YAML refuses it otherwise).

Reynolds and Mach numbers

Study levels (Stage 0)

1 × 10⁵ · 3 × 10⁵ · 1.5 × 10⁶ · 3 × 10⁶

On the mean chord. Every mesh study runs at these four. 1 × 10⁵ added 30 Oct 2026 for mini Class I wings.

Real wings fly at

1.2 × 10⁵ – 2.7 × 10⁶

Mean chord, cruise at 3,048 m to top speed at sea level, for the real wings with a published area.

Mach

0.03 – 0.20

Every type, both spaces: below 0.3, so the flow is incompressible to a good approximation. Speed comes from the real wings, not from the wing size.

Lowest: smallest chord at the family's lowest cruise speed at 3,048 m. Highest: largest chord at its highest top speed at sea level. Air from Stage 0 (ISA, Sutherland); a = 328.6 m/s at 3,048 m, 340.3 m/s at sea level. One wing covers a much narrower band than its row. Below the lowest study level (1 × 10⁵): only tips and the smallest wings at their slowest speed. Above the top one (3 × 10⁶): only the largest wings.

What each Re band means

Re (on the local chord)FlowWho is thereRANS (SA, fully turbulent)
below 10⁵Laminar; separation without reattachment is likely; strong hysteresisTips of small wings; full-space micro wingspoor no transition model, results only indicative
10⁵ – 5 × 10⁵Laminar separation bubbles, transition on the bubbleMost Class I wings; outer panels of BWBsbiased drag too high, bubble missed
5 × 10⁵ – 3 × 10⁶Transition ahead of mid-chord; mostly attached turbulent flowClass II wings; BWB centre bodiesgood small bias from the laminar run
above 3 × 10⁶Turbulent over most of the chordLargest full-space roots onlygood above the top study level

Bands are approximate (Carmichael 1981; Lissaman 1983; Mueller & DeLaurier 2003), see Flow phenomena.

Flow phenomena you will meet

What the flow does on these wings, at these Re and angles, and whether the planned CFD (ADflow, steady RANS, Spalart–Allmaras, fully turbulent) can see it.

PhenomenonWhere in our rangesWhat it doesDoes our CFD capture it?Source
Laminar flow, transition and laminar separation bubblesEvery type. Mean-chord Re 4 × 10⁴ – 3.4 × 10⁶; most BWB and mini Class I wings sit below 10⁶. Our low-Re sections (MH 45, MH 60, MH 61, MH 104) are designed for long laminar runs.Drag and lift depend on where the boundary layer turns turbulent. A bubble adds drag; at high angle it can burst, giving abrupt stall and hysteresis. Small changes in turbulence or roughness move the result.No. Spalart–Allmaras without transition makes the wall flow turbulent from the nose, so drag is biased. Carried as a model band (Stage 0); SU2 γ-Reθ is the planned check.Carmichael 1981 (NASA CR-165803); Lissaman 1983 (Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 15); Mueller & DeLaurier 2003 (Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 35)
Very low Re at the tipsBWB tip chords 3.5–16 cm: tip Re down to 2 × 10⁴. Tapered and cranked tips down to 2–3 × 10⁴ on the smallest wings.Thick laminar boundary layers and early separation at the tip, where the vortex forms.Weakly. Same model limit as above, at its worst. The first-cell law must use the local chord, not the mean chord.Same as above; first-cell law: Grand Roadmap R-V.1
Wake behind the trailing edgeEvery wing, the whole span. At 12° the wake leaves the edge at an angle; behind a blunt base it starts wide.A thin sheet of slow air: the boundary layers of both surfaces leave the edge and carry the profile drag downstream. It sets the pressure at the trailing edge and base, and it rolls up toward the tips.Only if the wake has its own cells. The S8 O-mesh has none: its cells grow fast behind the edge, so the wake smears. In AERIS, refining the near wake alone moved base drag by 23 counts. Plan: an overset wake box.Primer section 05; Chan et al. 2002
Tip vortex, roll-up and induced dragEvery wing; strongest at low aspect ratio (BWB down to 2.7) and high lift.The wake sheet rolls up into one vortex per tip within about one chord. It causes the downwash and the induced drag, a large share of the total.Yes, if the vortex keeps fine cells along its path. Plan: the roll-up inside the near-body mesh, then a vortex tube from about 2 chords behind the tip.Primer section 05
Sweep: spanwise flow, tip or root stall, pitch-upBWB 5–40° and flying wing 10–40° (aft); cranked and tapered −5° to +15° (forward to aft).Aft sweep pushes the boundary layer outboard, so the tip stalls first and the nose can pitch up. Forward sweep stalls the root first.Spanwise flow: yes. Stall onset and pitch-up: less reliable with steady RANS near maximum lift.Standard swept-wing aerodynamics
Panel breaks (kinks) at b1 and b2Every BWB and cranked wing; tapered wings have no break in the edges.Local suction peaks and a jump in the span loading at the break; a ruled loft has a slope break there.Yes, if a mesh station sits exactly on each break (fix 3). Otherwise flat faces cut the corner.Loft decision (kSpan 2)
Separation and stall at high angleThe 12° study angle, and 8° on thin or strongly cambered sections at low Re.Trailing-edge or leading-edge separation, unsteady flow, maximum lift.Steady RANS gives a number but is not reliable near maximum lift; convergence is harder. Keep 12° for the nose and wake studies only.Stage 0 angles 0 / 4 / 8 / 12°
Blunt trailing edge: base flowEvery wing: thickness max(0.5 mm, 0.2 % of chord) (Class I).A base pressure drag and, in reality, vortex shedding behind the base.Partly. Steady RANS damps the shedding. At 0.2 % with 8 cells the base was 2–4 % of pressure drag (measured in AERIS).Primer section 03; Papadakis & Manolesos 2020 (flatback, RANS damps shedding)
Low Mach numberTop speed 67 m/s: Mach ≤ 0.20 (BWB ≤ 0.12).The air is nearly incompressible.The compressible solver needs low-speed preconditioning; without it ADflow did not converge in AERIS.Primer track 3
Slender, flexible wingsCranked and tapered aspect ratio up to 16.5.Long thin wings bend and twist in flight, which changes the span loading.No. The CFD wing is rigid. Many span stations are needed.Outside this study (no aeroelasticity)
The biggest one. Most of these wings fly where transition and laminar bubbles set the drag, and the planned model cannot see them. Mesh error can be made small; this model error cannot. Every drag number needs its model band, and differences between wings are safer than absolute drag.

Where the mesh must be fine

Each phenomenon above lives in one region of the flow; each region gets its own rule. The rules are the Grand Roadmap recipes (R-S, R-V) and the Stage 0 error budget: the share is how much of the 65 % grid error each direction may use. The last column says where S8 stands today.

ZoneCapturesRule (starting value)Budget shareSourceS8 today
Wall-normal, every wallBoundary layer, skin friction, separation; transition if a transition model is runFirst cell from y⁺ ≤ 1 at each station's own Re (local chord), so small tips get their own; growth ≤ 1.25 inside the boundary layer, ≤ 1.3 outside; ≥ 30 cells across the boundary layerwall-normal 20 %Roadmap R-V.1, R-V.2 (laws 13, 14); DPW gridding guidelinesOne first cell (4.71 µm) for every station; growth 1.253; 29 cells across the boundary layer
Leading edge (nose)Suction peak, start of the laminar run, stall at 12°Chordwise spacing solved so no cell turns the surface by more than 10° (ladder 12 / 10 / 8 / 6°); nose cells of neighbouring stations differ by at most 15 %chordwise 35 %Roadmap R-S.5, R-S.6 (laws 1, 2)In place
Upper surface, about 30–60 % chordLaminar separation bubble and transitionOnly with a transition model: fine chordwise cells over the bubble and a cap on growth along the ring (≤ 1.25). With fully turbulent SA there is no bubble to resolvechordwise 35 %Our choice; depends on the transition route (Stage 0 D5)Not done
Trailing edge and blunt baseBase drag, base flow, start of the wakeChordwise spacing 0.1 % of local chord at the edge; 8 cells (9 points) across the base at the coarse leveledges and base 15 %Roadmap R-S.3, R-S.4 (laws 3, 6); DPW (8/12/16/24 cells), SPICES (≥ 8 at the fine level)In place (family 3)

Near wake, trailing edge to 2 chordsWake sheet (velocity deficit), base flow, start of roll-upOverset wake box with cells of 0.0075 c (about 20 across the wake), tall and tilted to hold the wake at 0–12°; starts inside the near-body meshwake 15 %Roadmap R-V.6 (laws 17, 18); Chan et al. 2002No designed wake (O-mesh)

Overlap between meshesNothing leaks: the wake and the boundary layer pass between grids cleanly≥ 5 cells from each mesh, cell-size ratio ≤ 1.5, no overlap inside the boundary layer or at the tip, 0 orphan cells—Roadmap R-V.7 (law 21); Chan et al. 2002; Kenway et al. 2017Not built yet (Stage 2, M3)

Budget shares from Stage 0: chordwise 35 %, spanwise 15 %, wall-normal 20 %, edges and base 15 %, wake 15 % of the grid error; domain 10 % of the total. All values are starting values; the mesh studies (Grand Roadmap stage 4) confirm or replace them.

Fix left (for Stage 2)

Done on 29 Oct 2026: the unrealistic conventional set (tapered type and per-panel chords), the dihedral input (three panel values) and the hash (from the code itself). One fix is left, and it belongs to Stage 2.

  1. The loft has sharp kinks at b1, b2 and the switch sections.Correct for straight panels, but the S8 mesher does not place stations at the breaks. Flat mesh faces would then cut the corner, about 0.5 % of chord (a rough estimate). Do: Stage 2 must put a mesh station exactly at every station_v. No change here; put it in the Stage 2 prompt.

One wing, step by step

Seven steps: design vector, planform, sections, twist and dihedral, trailing edge, loft, measure-label-check. Example: a BWB with every variable at mid-range.

The Aquila (taper 0.58, sweep 28°) fitted no type, and plain swept flying wings are the most common small tailless UAVs. Decided 29 Oct 2026.Your rule
D3Same 18 variables for every typeEach type samples some and derives the rest (see Inputs and derived).One vector shape for sampling, hashing and ML.Our choice
D4Everything variesA value is fixed only through pinned:.A study may pin; the default never does.Your rule
D5Size inputs: root chord and aspect ratiospan_mode: aspect_ratio for every type. The semi-span follows: S = AR · c_root · K / 2, K = mean chord / root chord.Drawing the span on its own let wings with a tail reach AR 21 (13 % above 16.5, the highest real value). Drawing AR keeps every wing inside the real range by construction, with no refusals. Decided 29 Oct 2026.Your rule
D6Chord lawstations: c2, c3, c4 as fractions of the root (BWB). per_panel: each panel's own taper, at most 1 (cranked). linear_taper: one taper, c2 and c3 follow (tapered, flying wing).Before, 46 of 100 conventional wings got wider toward the tip. With per-panel ratios no chord grows outboard, and the Latin hypercube stays intact.Your rule
D7Sweep lawpanels: one sweep per panel. one: sweep2 = sweep3 = sweep1 (tapered, flying wing).Straight leading edge for straight-edged wings. Variables a law computes need no range.Your rule
D8Size ranges from real wingsRoot chord: BWB 0.40–1.80 m; cranked and tapered 0.13–0.75 m; flying wing 0.25–1.05 m. AR: tailless 3–9; with a tail 4.5–16.5.All 27 real wings with a published area (makers, papers, theses; Class II from Götten et al. 2021, Essari 2015 and the AUTh RX-3 BWB) have a generated wing within 10 % in span and mean chord, and all 62 real spans are inside (see Real wings). BWB root raised from 0.80 to 1.80 m on 30 Oct 2026: the old range was sized on small flying wings and missed real BWBs (RX-3: 4.9 m², 260 kg; Wang & Zhou: root 1.80 m).Measured
D9Shape ranges from sourcesEvery range has its basis in the Why this range column and in decisions/shape_ranges.md. Changed on 29 Oct 2026: tailed sweep −5° to +15° (was −10° to +20°); tailed washout at most 5° (was 7°); dihedral 0–5° for every type (Raymer); flying-wing taper 0.3–0.9 and sweep 10–40°; BWB tip down to 0.06, first sweep from 15°.Each range now rests on a design rule (Raymer) or on a published small UAV (BWB: Wang & Zhou 2022, Suewatanakul 2022, Lehmkuehler 2012, Hainline 2017; flying wing: Milenković-Babić 2024, Panknin, PUL-10, a flying-wing MAV). Layout shares (b3, split) remain our choice. BlendedNet is a larger Group 3 BWB and is not used for the ranges.Source
D10Two spaces: full and focusPer type, ranges + airfoils = the focus space (realistic, suggested); full_ranges + full_airfoils = the full space (everything supported). The focus box must lie inside the full box, and each suggested section must be a full candidate; the YAML is refused otherwise.Your rule (30 Oct 2026): design everything, but put the wings and the simulations densely where the real wings are. Full bounds are our choice: the widest value in any source, rounded out (e.g. BlendedNet sweeps 60°, Wang & Zhou root 1.8 m, Prandtl-D washout 10°).Your rule
D11Wing classwing_class: I | II sets the trailing-edge floor.Manufacturing differs by size.Your rule
Planform
D12Exact straight panelsLeading and trailing edges are straight lines through b0–b3. Chords and sweeps equal the vector exactly.The old AERIS spline put the b2 chord up to 20 % off; a 12°/6°/6° wing came out 7.9°/7.9°/6.5°.Measured
D13Signed sweepLeading-edge sweep, positive aft. Forward sweep is allowed by the ranges, not blocked by code.Conventional wings need it.Your rule
D14No curved BWB centre bodyNot in this stage. To add later with a check that rejects wavy edges.Straight panels first. So today's BWB is a cranked tailless wing with a long root chord.Our choice
Sections, twist, dihedral
D15Vertical sections; root in y = 0Every section is parallel to the symmetry plane and only twisted about its leading edge. The validity gate refuses a wing whose root leaves y = 0 by more than 1e-9 m, or any point that crosses y = 0.The two mirrored halves then meet exactly in the root section and never cross. AERIS (and its AVL path) rolled the root section with the first panel's dihedral, so the halves crossed and the root dihedral had to be pinned at zero. pyGeo only receives our section points, never a dihedral angle. Cost: on a panel with dihedral Γ the true thickness is cos Γ smaller (1.5 % at 10°).Your rule
D16One dihedral per panelInputs dihedral_p1, p2, p3. Station heights: zi = Σ tan(Γpanel) · panel span.Four station values gave only three panel slopes, so one input did nothing ([0, 3, 3, 6], [3, 0, 6, 3] and [1.5, 1.5, 4.5, 4.5] built the same wing). The gate now checks each panel dihedral against the vector. Fixed 29 Oct 2026.Your rule
D17TwistExact at the four stations; between them it follows the straight panel.Straight panels and linear twist cannot both hold. Difference 0.1–0.3 % of chord at the trailing edge.Measured
D18Aspect ratio exact with twistThe mean chord K counts the true chord of a straight panel: where the twist changes, the chord turns and is a little shorter mid-panel (0.6 % for a 13° change). K = Σ fi ∫ |chord vector| dt, 32-point Gauss.Found by the full-space sets: with washout up to 12°, 4 wings missed their aspect ratio by 0.11–0.24 % (gate limit 0.1 %). Two causes: K assumed a linear chord, and the extra section at the trailing-edge switch took the linear chord and twist, so it sat off the straight panel. Both fixed 30 Oct 2026: the switch section now sits on the ruled panel (true chord and its twist). Worst aspect-ratio error on 730 built wings: 0.00004 %.Measured
Airfoils
D19Supported vs suggested sectionsSupported: any section in the database (2,159 files), in geometry/airfoils/, or a NACA 4/5-digit formula. Suggested: the per-type list from papers (focus space). The full space draws from every sourced section, on any type.Your rule (30 Oct 2026). A suggestion must have a source; support needs only a readable file.Your rule
D20Any airfoil by name OpenSearch order: geometry/airfoils/ → AERIS database (2,159 of 2,181 files load) → NACA 4/5-digit formula. A station may list candidates; the sampler draws them evenly. One wing may carry its own four names.BlendedNet (NACA 25118), M6, RIBES and CRM need sections outside the default list.Our choice
D21Default sectionsBWB: MH 104 body (15 %), MH 61 wing (10 %). Cranked and tapered: NACA 4415, 4415, 4412, 4412. Flying wing: MH 60 inboard, MH 45 outboard.BWB pair from a small BWB UAV (Suewatanakul et al. 2022). The old AERIS MH 91 is a paraglider section and NLF(1)-1015 a HALE section (Re 0.7–2 × 10⁶), so both were dropped. NACA 4415 flies on the Pioneer and the Shadow 200 (Lednicer). MH 45 and MH 60 are Hepperle's tailless sections; MH 60 suits Re ≥ 1.5 × 10⁵ (root), MH 45 lower Re (tip). Changed 29 Oct 2026.Source
D22One way to read every fileLeading edge = the point farthest from the trailing-edge midpoint; unit chord; both sides resampled on cosine x, in √x.The nose tangent is square to the chord, and every section has the same points, so the loft can join them.Our choice
D23Typo points droppedA single point that spikes off a smooth line is removed (18 database files, e.g. sc20412 at x/c 0.73).One bad point would put a bump in the surface. Kept by your decision on 29 Oct 2026; each dropped point is logged.Your rule
Trailing edge
D24Thickness rule OpenClass I: max(0.5 mm, 0.2 % of local chord). Class II: max(1.0 mm, 0.2 %).Real wings are blunt. In AERIS, 0.5 % carried about a fifth of the pressure drag; 0.2 % with 8 base cells carried 2–4 %. 0.2 % is also pyGeo's default. The floors still need a builder's confirmation.Measured
D25Made in the generatorOn the 2-D airfoil, before the loft. Not in the mesher.AVL, CFD and CAD see one wing. The AERIS mesher made 4.3 mm at one root, 2.4 times the rule, and moved lift 11–30 counts.Measured
D26How it openspyGeo's method: linear ramp from x/c = 0.90 to the edge, half up, half down. Camber line unchanged.Same as readAirfoilFile(bluntTe=True, bluntThickness=0.002, bluntTaperRange=0.1). Replaced the uncited 65 % start in v0.4. Cost: a 0.6° slope change at 90 % chord.Source
D27The rule wins over the fileA file with its own blunt edge is set to the rule (NACA 4415: 0.32 % → rule). Published wings keep theirs (as_is).Sampled wings follow one rule; copies of real wings stay real.Our choice
D28Extra section at the switchWhere the chord equals 0.25 m (Class I) or 0.5 m (Class II), a section is added.The loft blends thickness linearly; without it the edge would dip below the floor.Our choice
Loft (the surface the mesher reads)
D29Straight panels: kSpan = 2 FixSections only at b0–b3 plus switch points.kSpan 3 cut the corners at panel breaks by up to 4.8 % of chord; kSpan 2 is exact. It leaves a sharp kink at b1 and b2: see the one fix left.Measured
D30Built with pySpline, one parameter s = √(x/c)Same construction as pyGeo's liftingSurface, held in a pyGeo object.liftingSurface split upper and lower 0.2–0.5 % of chord away from the nose. Here the split is exact and u = x/c on every station.Measured
D31Ask, never interpolateThe mesher asks upper(u, v) and lower(u, v); a 401-point table maps v to span.In AERIS, straight lines between stored sections missed the surface by up to 7.25 % of chord (ADR-0015).Measured
D32TipFlat and open (tip='none').Rounded tips are a later study.Our choice
D33Two backends, one exportpyGeo (production, IGES) and numpy (same surface, no pyGeo). No STEP: pyGeo has no STEP writer.Tests and pictures run anywhere.Our choice
Measure, label, hash
D34Measured on the loftChord, twist, LE position, sweep, dihedral, area, span, MAC, AR, thickness, trailing-edge thickness → measured.json. The gate checks chords, sweeps, twists, panel dihedrals and the aspect ratio against the vector.Later stages and any ML model use the measured wing; the vector is only its label.Your rule
D35Labels by ruleConfiguration: bwb (measured centre body), else flying_wing for a tailless type or conventional for a type with a tail. Then swept, cranked, rectangular, washout, dihedral, aspect ratio. BWB threshold 2.2.A tail is not part of the wing surface, so it cannot be measured; the family comes from the type. Before 29 Oct 2026 every tailless wing without a centre body was called 'conventional'. Checked on 20 hand-labelled wings and a flying-wing test.Your rule
D36Hash from the code itselfsha256 of the vector (with its four section names), the type's laws and pinned values (not its ranges), the trailing-edge rule, the airfoil coordinates and the content of every geometry source file.Any code change now changes every input hash, so stored meshes and results are never reused for a wing the code builds differently. A version string set by hand could be forgotten. Fixed 29 Oct 2026.Your rule
Sets
D37Seven sets per type, two spacesFocus: training 100 (Latin hypercube, seeds 1001–1004), reference 5 (by rule), hold-out 10 (seeds 2001–2004). Full: training 40 (seeds 1101–1104), hold-out 5 (seeds 2101–2104), corner 1 (each free variable at each full bound: 34 or 26 wings) and corner 2 (every pair at all four low/high combinations: 8 or 7).Dense where real wings are, sparse over everything we support; the corners test the edges of what we claim. The hold-outs are the honest tests. Decided 30 Oct 2026.Your rule
D38Failures stay in the listA refused wing keeps its row with the gate and the reason. Corners are never nudged inside.A failure marks the edge of the space.Your rule
D39Hold-out is never built hereOnly the vectors are saved.It is opened once, after the workflow is frozen.Your rule
D40Reference wings spread wellCoverage distance BWB 1.51, cranked 1.45, tapered 1.31, flying wing 1.35, against a median of 1.82 / 1.79 / 1.62 / 1.59 for 1,000 random sets of five (lower is better).Five wings must stand for the whole set.Measured

Real wings and the Reynolds number

Your rule (29 Oct 2026): take the sizes from real Class I and II UAVs, compute the Re they fly at, and if it does not reach 5 × 10⁶, lower the top Re level instead of stretching the wings. Data and links: configs/real_uavs.yaml; check: scripts/real_uav_check.py.

Real wings fly at

Re 1.2 × 10⁵ – 2.7 × 10⁶

Lowest: Black Swift S0 cruising at 3,048 m. Highest: RUAG Ranger at top speed, sea level. Mean chord = wing area / span.

So the top Re level

5 × 10⁶ → 3 × 10⁶

No wing of our families reaches 5 × 10⁶. Only the Sperwer (a delta) and the Vindicator (a target drone above Mach 0.3) do. Levels now 3 × 10⁵, 1.5 × 10⁶, 3 × 10⁶ (the highest real value, 2.74 × 10⁶ for the RUAG Ranger at top speed, rounded up).

Generator covers them

27 of 27 real wings

Each real wing with a published area has a generated wing within 10 % in span and mean chord. Every Class I span is inside too (sourced and HCDI database). BWB span 0.6–8.2 m, mean chord 0.17–1.06 m; conventional span 0.5–10.4 m, mean chord 0.10–0.71 m.

Class II

Chords 0.55–0.66 m

Nine Class II wings with an area: Götten et al. 2021 (from images and three-views, about 10–15 %) and Essari 2015 (Jane's-style: Hermes 450, Ranger, Seeker, Shadow 600). AR 7.8–16. At top speed, Re 2.1–2.7 × 10⁶. Gap: tailless Class II has no area.

Clouds: 2,000 generated wings per type (green BWB, blue conventional and tapered). Red: real wings with a published area. Dotted lines: real wings with a published span only.

Checks and results

Gate 1 · vector → loft

Measured on the loft: chords within 0.1 %, sweeps 0.1°, twist 0.2°, dihedral 0.2°.

Gate 2 · trailing edge

Thickness equals the rule at every section, within 1 µm.

Gate 3 · validity

Sections closed, upper never below lower, root flat in y = 0 within 1e-9 m, chords positive.

Gate 4 · repeatability

Two builds give the same surface hash.

A wing that fails any gate is not written; its row keeps the gate and the reason. The fifth check, mesh on the loft within 1e-9 m, belongs to Stage 2.

Is the loft the designed wing? (every sampled wing)

Worst value over every training, corner and reference wing (scripts/verify_sets.py, numpy loft). Stations, chords, twists, sweeps, panel dihedrals and the straightness of each panel match the inputs to machine precision. AR: the loft measures the true chord, which is a little shorter between two stations of different twist (up to 0.035 %; 0 without twist). Sections: up to 0.012 % of chord, at the smallest tips, where the 0.5 mm trailing-edge floor is a large share of a 3 cm chord. Root: every point of the root section at y = 0, and no point of a half wing below y = 0, so the mirrored halves meet only there.

Open decisions

Choices made to keep going that still need your call.

  • Tailless Class II chords. Flying-wing spans now reach 7.7 m, so Fury (5.2 m), Albatroz (7 m) and Shahed 191 (7.3 m) are inside by span. Their areas are unknown, so the chord is unchecked.
  • Smallest wings. Kept by your decision (29 Oct 2026): generated spans start at 0.4–0.6 m (micro Class I).
  • NTNU UAV database. 93 UAVs with span, AR and estimated chord (DataverseNO, CC0). Blocked from the cloud workspace: attach 02_Database.csv to add it.
  • Essari 2015 data. Hermes 450, Ranger, Seeker, Shadow 600 areas come from a PhD thesis citing unread (Jane's-style) references; its Hermes 450 is internally inconsistent (0.69 m × 10.51 m = 7.25 m², listed 6.90). Confirm with Jane's before the paper.
  • Re levels. Now 3 × 10⁵, 1.5 × 10⁶, 3 × 10⁶. Move the middle to about 9.5 × 10⁵ (log-middle)? Mini Class I wings fly at 1.2–2 × 10⁵, below the lowest level.
  • Closest prior work. Pliakos et al. 2025 (AUTh: Eng. Proc. 90:52 and Algorithms 18:186) automate the same chain for UAV wings: OpenVSP → ANSA → Fluent, 2 panels, ONERA M6 only, no transition model. The paper must state what we add (4 stations / 3 panels, two spaces, refusing gates, transition-aware Re bands, open tools).
  • AUTh BWB airfoils and chords. Their BWB airfoils and station chords sit in paywalled papers (AST 2018, AST 2021, AIAA 2020/2022, ICUAS 2020). Get them through the Patras library or ask the authors.
  • Full-space edges. The full space reaches 20 m span and Re 7.6 × 10⁶ on the largest BWB root: beyond Class II and above the top study level. Keep, or cap the span?
  • Transition check. ADflow (MACH-Aero) has no transition model; SA is its only differentiated and tested model (Menter SST runs, no adjoint). Plan: SU2 γ-Reθ on a few reference wings at 1 × 10⁵ and 3 × 10⁵, on a y+ ≤ 1 mesh, to size the model band.
  • Second-hand sources. Raymer's taper 0.4 and washout −3° are quoted from a course page; PUL-10 and the flying-wing MAV were read by the research agent only. Check them in print before the paper.
  • Trailing-edge floor. Confirm 0.5 mm / 1.0 mm with the builder. Run the 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 % sensitivity once CFD works.
  • Airfoil search order. Project folder → AERIS database → NACA formula. Keep? 22 database files are refused.
  • NACA 25118 trailing edge. Made from the formula (open edge, 0.38 %). OpenVSP may close it differently. Check with a BlendedNet STEP file.
  • NASA CRM. Four stations and stand-in sections: a shape check only, or add a many-station mode for drag validation?
  • BlendedNet twist and dihedral. Set to zero because neither paper states them. Accept?
  • Which published wing first. RIBES is the only in-regime case; M6 and CRM are transonic.
  • RIBES trailing edge. The fitted section has 0.26 %; the model measures 0.38–0.66 %. Rebuild before any drag comparison?
  • Outside proof. Only the M6 is checked against its own CAD (max 0.011 % of chord). BlendedNet, CRM and RIBES need their surface files.

What it cannot make (yet)

  • Straight edges only, three panels at most. No curved BWB centre body, no elliptic planform, no fourth panel.
  • Airfoil shape is not a variable. Any named file can be used, and a station can draw from a list, but thickness and camber are not sampled continuously. The default sets use one section per station (t/c 10–15 %).
  • No winglets, rounded or raked tips, fuselage, gaps. Panel dihedral 0–5° for every type: no anhedral.
  • Some shape sources are thin. The layout shares (where b1 and b2 sit) are our choice. A few rules are second-hand (Raymer via a course page). BWB shapes rest on four small-UAV papers, two of them larger than Class I.
  • Class II areas are uncertain. They rest on Götten et al. (from photos, about 10–15 %) and a thesis citing unread Jane's-style data. Tailless Class II have no area at all.
  • 0 refusals at the corners. The space is too safe to show where anything breaks. Robustness must be shown on the mesher, with lofts it has never seen (primer Track 5).
  • Published wings: M6 and CRM are transonic (phase 1 stops at Mach 0.3). CRM is approximate. BlendedNet twist and dihedral are guessed as zero. Every tip is a flat cut, including the M6's rounded one.

python scripts/verify_geometry.py                                    # is the surface the intended wing?
